Consult Summary:
65-year-old male with acute, ongoing central chest pressure radiating to left arm/shoulder, associated nausea, diaphoresis, dyspnea; high clinical concern for acute coronary syndrome.  Ambulance arranged for immediate transfer; clinician remained on call until arrival.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute chest pain – rule out acute coronary syndrome
- Onset: ~2 hours ago while gardening (light activity).
- Character: Diffuse “pressure,” “someone sitting on chest.”
- Radiation: Left arm and shoulder.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), diaphoresis, shortness of breath, subjective tachycardia/palpitations.
- Persisting at time of call.
- Risk factors: Male, 65 y; current smoker (10 cigarettes/day × 15 yrs); hypertension; overweight; limited exercise; family history—father fatal MI ~60 y, mother “heart problems.”
- No prior similar episodes.
- Clinical impression: Suspected myocardial infarction; ambulance dispatched for emergent evaluation (ECG, possible hospital admission).

Issue 2: Hypertension
- Patient-reported history of high blood pressure; current control and medications not documented.
- Cardiovascular risk compounded by smoking, alcohol use, overweight, probable dyslipidemia (never tested).

Issue 3: Tobacco and alcohol use
- Smoking: 10 cigarettes/day for 15 years.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints beer/week.
- Brief assessment only; cessation advice deferred due to acute event.

Medications:
- None documented (antihypertensive therapy status unknown; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Aspirin – allergic swelling (mild); not life-threatening but clinically relevant.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension.
- Overweight/obesity (self-reported).
- No known diabetes; cholesterol never checked.

Social History:
- Lives alone; front door open for ambulance access.
- Occupation: Sushi restaurant owner.
- Smoking: 10 cigarettes/day × 15 yrs.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints beer/week.
- Low regular physical activity.

Preventative History:
- No documentation of cardiovascular screening, vaccinations, cancer screening, or other preventive care.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals or physical exam performed.

Plan:
- Ambulance requested; clinician remained on call until arrival.
- Pre-hospital team to perform ECG and decide destination hospital.
- Patient instructed to leave front door open for access.
- Patient to inform ambulance/hospital staff of aspirin allergy (may require aspirin administration despite mild reaction).
- Hospital evaluation to include ECG, cardiac enzymes, and management per ACS protocol.
- Subsequent outpatient follow-up (post-discharge) to address hypertension management, lipid profile, smoking cessation, weight, and alcohol intake.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements: Current medication list, vital signs, detailed cardiovascular exam, lipid profile, diabetes screening, vaccination status, cancer screening history.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minimal background noise; no significant inaudible sections.
